title: Observability guardrails: resource quotas, alert throttling, and safe schema migrations for private installs
author: Maya Chen
release_notes:
- Enforce per-tenant Prometheus Alertmanager rate limits and silencing defaults.
- Add cluster-level and tenant-level resource quota CRDs for observability components (Prometheus/Grafana/Fluentd).
- Introduce a zero-downtime Grafana schema migration path with validation and rollback hooks.
description:
Context and motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in constrained on-prem or VPC environments have reported incidents where a misconfigured tenant or imported dashboard caused observability components to saturate cluster resources or spam Alertmanager with noisy alerts during upgrades. This PR introduces a set of conservative guardrails that prevent single-tenant misconfiguration from impacting the control plane and adds a safe migration path for Grafana schema changes.

What this PR does (summary): Adds tenant-aware ResourceQuota and LimitRange templating for observability Helm charts; integrates a configurable Alertmanager receiver throttling policy and default inhibition rules; implements a migration operator that performs schema validation against a pre-upgrade snapshot and exposes an explicit safe-apply + rollback flow for Grafana dashboards and database migrations.

Checklist implemented: - [x] Helm chart changes for prometheus-operator and grafana to support quota templating and quota-aware values. - [x] New CRD: ObservabilityTenantQuota (lightweight wrapper to express tenant quota hints). - [x] Alertmanager throttling defaults and templates, with opt-out via values.yaml. - [x] Migration operator that snapshots Grafana DB before applying migrations and runs dry-run validation. - [x] Integration tests for quota injection and alert throttling behavior in CI. - [x] Documentation and upgrade notes in private-installer/UPGRADING.md.

Commits (high level): - 7f4c1a2: Add ObservabilityTenantQuota CRD and controller scaffolding. - b3d2e13: Helm: parameterize prometheus-operator and grafana charts to consume tenant quotas. - 4c9e2ff: Alertmanager: add receiver throttling template and default inhibition rule set. - a9d0b7c: Migration operator: snapshot, validate, migrate, rollback actions. - e2f8a01: CI: add observability-guardrails integration test job and fixtures.

Files/areas changed (high level): - helm/prometheus/templates/limits.yaml: templated ResourceQuota/LimitRange entries and notes for fine-tuning. - helm/grafana/templates/migration-hooks.yaml: pre/post hooks to trigger snapshot and migrate. - charts/migration-operator/{deployment,rbac,crd}: operator that orchestrates safe migrations and snapshots. - manifests/crds/observabilitytenantquota.yaml: CRD definition and sample. - docs/observability-guardrails.md and UPGRADING.md: upgrade path and recommended settings. - test/integration/observability-guardrails/: end-to-end tests that simulate noisy tenant behavior.

Review conversation summary: - Diego Rivera: requested stronger defaults for quota values and a safe fail-open option. Action: added conservative defaults and a feature flag 'observability.failOpenOnQuotaExceed' to allow emergency operator bypass. - Priya Nair: raised concern about Alertmanager route complexity and suggested adding observability-level circuit breakers. Action: added a route-level throttle and a per-tenant cumulative receiver cap; documented tradeoffs. - Samir Patel: asked for explicit instrumentation to measure throttling hits and quota rejections. Action: added metrics prometheus_operator_quota_rejections_total and alertmanager_throttle_events_total and wired them into the observability dashboards. - Follow-ups: small nits fixed (naming, unit tests) and one test flake addressed by increasing a readiness timeout in the migration operator tests.

CI and validation: - The PR wired a new integration job 'integration/observability-guardrails' that spins up a lightweight KinD cluster and exercises quota injection, alert throttling under simulated noisy alerts, and migration dry-runs. - CI initially failed on a flaky migration test (timeout); rerun passed. Final CI status: pass.

Backward compatibility and upgrade strategy: - This change is opt-in for existing tenants by defaulting the new quota enforcement to 'monitor-only' mode. The operator will emit quota_rejection metrics but will not block apply unless customers set enforcement=true in values. - Grafana schema migrations run behind the migration-operator; default behavior is dry-run validation plus operator approval. Explicit 'apply' flag is required in the private-installer values to perform changes. - Documented step-by-step upgrade procedure included in UPGRADING.md to minimize surprises for air-gapped installs.

Testing performed: - Unit tests for CRD validation and controller reconciliation. - Integration tests covering: quota templating injection, Alertmanager throttling under simulated burst, and a full migration scenario that snapshots and rolls back on validation failures. - Manual validation on a 3-node on-prem staging tenant showing no resource exhaustion when importing a large dashboard bundle.

Operational notes: - Added Grafana dashboard panel 'Observability Guardrails' to show quota budgets, enforced limits, throttle events, and snapshot status. - Added runbook snippet for on-call: how to temporarily flip failOpenOnQuotaExceed to true and how to trigger a rollback of a Grafana migration via the operator CLI.

Merge outcome: After two approvals (Diego and Priya) and CI green, the PR was squash-merged to main on 2026-02-24. Release: changes will be included in the next private-installer point release and called out in the release notes for operators performing upgrades.

Related work and follow-ups: - TODO: expose an API endpoint for solutions engineers to query tenant quota consumption across private clusters (follow-up ENG-8581). - TODO: add optional automatic alert suppression heuristics for known noisy exporters (SRE-328).

If you want to test locally: follow docs/observability-guardrails.md; run the provided KinD scripts in test/integration/observability-guardrails/; use the migration-operator binary with the '--dry-run' flag to validate migrations before applying.
